title: Errors: throws, do/catch, Result and rethrows

videos.script: A student types forty where a number should be. The planner has to say what went wrong, not only that something did. {{throws}} In Swift, a function that can fail says so in its declaration, with the word throws. And every call to it is marked with try, so you see where failure can come from. {{catch}} Then do and catch. Each kind of failure gets its own clause, and the program carries on. {{variants}} Then the two shortcuts. Try with a question mark turns an error into nil. Try with an exclamation mark turns it into a crash, and you will see one. {{typed}} Since Swift 6, a function can name the one error type it throws, and the compiler checks every case. {{result}} Then Result, an error you can keep in a variable and look at later. {{rethrows}} And last, rethrows, for functions that fail only when their closure does, and defer, the cleanup that runs on every way out.
